scope.breadth_policy: depth-only; Volume 420 remains the last top-level volume
scope.purpose: Close adversarial cross-condition proof gaps that single-dimension engineering checks can miss.

governing_rule: A package cannot reach verified, hardened, or production maturity by satisfying independent dimensions while an applicable cross-condition adversarial obligation remains unresolved.

closure_axes.name: Bootstrap and root trust
closure_axes.gap: The plan specified steady-state authority better than first-start/re-root behavior.
adversarial_questions: What establishes the first trusted state on an empty machine?
Can stale or compromised trust roots survive repair/reinstall?
Can safe mode start when normal dependencies are unavailable?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Promotion stops if initial trust, re-root, or dependency-reduced bootstrap is implicit.

closure_axes.name: Quiescence, shutdown, and restart
closure_axes.gap: Cancellation existed, but drain/shutdown boundaries could still lose or duplicate committed work.
adversarial_questions: What may still commit after shutdown begins?
How are in-flight effects drained, fenced, or resumed?
Is restart behavior deterministic at every lifecycle state?
closure_axes.stop_condition: No hardened claim while shutdown can strand authority or repeat a side effect.

closure_axes.name: Hard resource exhaustion
closure_axes.gap: Backpressure existed, but hard exhaustion needed explicit ENOSPC/OOM/FD/quota/token behavior.
adversarial_questions: What happens at zero free disk, memory, descriptors, quota, credits, or context budget?
Which control plane remains alive under saturation?
Are emergency reserves themselves bounded and tested?
closure_axes.stop_condition: A package cannot be production-ready if exhaustion becomes corruption, deadlock, or unbounded retry.

closure_axes.name: Dependency degradation and capability contraction
closure_axes.gap: Fallback paths can accidentally widen authority, privacy, cost, or semantics.
adversarial_questions: Does fallback preserve or narrow authority and data residency?
What capabilities disappear when a dependency degrades?
Can stale health cause oscillation or fallback storms?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Fallback may not silently increase privilege, data exposure, or irreversible behavior.

closure_axes.name: Unknown external outcome
closure_axes.gap: Timeout after a remote side effect can leave success/failure unknowable.
adversarial_questions: How is timeout-after-commit distinguished from timeout-before-commit?
Is retry blocked until reconciliation?
Can receipts be reconstructed from provider state?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Unknown side-effect outcome must enter reconciliation, not blind retry.

closure_axes.name: Reconciliation, duplicates, and orphans
closure_axes.gap: Distributed and long-running work creates orphaned jobs, duplicate messages, and divergent projections.
adversarial_questions: How are orphaned jobs/artifacts/locks detected?
Which authority wins after projection divergence?
Can reconciliation itself repeat an effect?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Every durable projection/effect path must have a bounded reconciliation story.

closure_axes.name: Mixed-version migration and rollback
closure_axes.gap: Migration rules existed, but old/new reader-writer coexistence needed explicit adversarial proof.
adversarial_questions: What if old readers observe new writes?
What if rollback occurs after a one-way transform?
Can feature flags create incompatible mixed states?
closure_axes.stop_condition: No strong promotion without a proven mixed-version window or an explicit stop-the-world contract.

closure_axes.name: Restore versus deletion and external reality
closure_axes.gap: Backup restore can resurrect deleted state or disagree with external side effects.
adversarial_questions: Can restore resurrect tombstoned data?
How are external effects reconciled after point-in-time restore?
Do restored credentials/leases remain valid?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Restore is incomplete until deletion, identity, leases, and external effects are reconciled.

closure_axes.name: Time, expiry, and lease semantics
closure_axes.gap: Wall clock, monotonic time, TTLs, leases, and ordering can disagree under skew or rollback.
adversarial_questions: What uses monotonic versus wall clock?
What happens on clock rollback/jump or long suspend?
Can expiry or lease checks disagree across nodes?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Time-dependent authorization or ownership must not rely on unqualified wall-clock assumptions.

closure_axes.name: Identity, credential, and key continuity
closure_axes.gap: Reinstall, restore, rotation, revocation, and delegated identity can break continuity or preserve stale power.
adversarial_questions: What survives reinstall or restore: identity, authority, neither?
Can revoked delegated credentials reappear from cache/checkpoint?
Can key rotation invalidate historical verification?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Stale or restored credentials may not regain authority without revalidation.

closure_axes.name: Semantic drift without version change
closure_axes.gap: Providers, models, tools, and remote APIs can change behavior while identifiers remain stable.
adversarial_questions: How is silent provider/tool semantic drift detected?
Which canaries distinguish model drift from data drift?
Does drift invalidate cached eval evidence?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Cached compatibility/eval claims expire when semantic canaries detect material drift.

closure_axes.name: Canonicalization, TOCTOU, and exact-resource execution
closure_axes.gap: Authorization can be correct for one representation and execution can touch another.
adversarial_questions: Is normalization complete before authorization?
Can symlinks/DNS/redirects/case/Unicode change the resource after approval?
Is the executed resource digest/identity bound to the decision?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Authorization must bind the exact normalized resource or immutable identity actually executed.

closure_axes.name: Hostile input and parser/resource bombs
closure_axes.gap: Valid-looking structured data can trigger pathological CPU, memory, recursion, decompression, or fan-out.
adversarial_questions: Are nested/recursive/decompression limits explicit?
Can one input create superlinear fan-out?
Are Unicode/confusable and ambiguous encodings normalized safely?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Input acceptance must be bounded by size, depth, expansion, and compute limits.

closure_axes.name: Evidence integrity and verifier independence
closure_axes.gap: A plan can appear complete when evidence is stale, self-produced, correlated, or detached from the artifact.
adversarial_questions: Does evidence bind code/config/environment/artifact/fault manifest?
Is high-impact verification independent of generation?
Can a rerun overwrite failed evidence?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Verified/hardened/production claims require artifact-bound, retained, independently checkable evidence.

closure_axes.name: Economic denial of service and budget overshoot
closure_axes.gap: Compute/cost limits can fail after admission through fan-out, retries, long outputs, or provider repricing.
adversarial_questions: Can actual cost exceed reserved budget after retries/fan-out?
What happens when provider price/rate limits change mid-operation?
Can one tenant starve shared budget or control capacity?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Budget overshoot must degrade or stop predictably before shared-service starvation.

closure_axes.name: Observability failure and telemetry pressure
closure_axes.gap: Telemetry itself can fail, backpressure the system, leak secrets, or erase the evidence needed for recovery.
adversarial_questions: What happens when logs/metrics/traces are unavailable?
Can cardinality or volume exhaust storage/memory?
Does redaction preserve enough evidence for reconstruction?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Core correctness may not depend on telemetry availability; critical recovery evidence must remain reconstructable.

closure_axes.name: Cross-tenant and cross-workspace isolation
closure_axes.gap: Isolation must survive caches, queues, indexes, retries, traces, artifacts, and evaluation fixtures.
adversarial_questions: Can shared caches/indexes return another tenant's data?
Do retries/dead letters preserve tenant identity?
Can telemetry/evals/artifacts cross workspace boundaries?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Tenant/workspace identity must be part of every authoritative lookup, cache key, receipt, and replay boundary.

closure_axes.name: Data lifecycle, rebuild, and compaction
closure_axes.gap: Derived data can outlive authority, deletion, schema, or source truth through backfills/reindex/compaction.
adversarial_questions: Does rebuild reapply current deletion and authorization policy?
Can compaction erase audit/provenance needed for proof?
Are derived indexes invalidated after source change?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Derived state must be rebuildable from authoritative inputs without resurrecting forbidden or stale data.

closure_axes.name: Human override, break-glass, and operator error
closure_axes.gap: Human control can become a bypass unless scope, fatigue, recovery, and post-use revocation are explicit.
adversarial_questions: Can break-glass authority exceed the minimum recovery need?
How is approval fatigue detected or bounded?
Can an operator undo/preview destructive recovery actions?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Human override is auditable, time-bounded, least-authority, and cannot erase evidence.

closure_axes.name: Plan, machine contract, and implementation drift
closure_axes.gap: Breadth freeze can hide omissions if prose, machine mirrors, code, tests, and runbooks diverge.
adversarial_questions: Does every claimed requirement map to a machine contract and evidence path?
Can code introduce undeclared authority or storage?
Are stale plan links detected automatically?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Promotion stops on unresolved target/current drift or machine/human contract disagreement.

closure_axes.name: Recovery dependency cycles and dependency-reduced safe mode
closure_axes.gap: A recovery plan can deadlock if the thing needed to recover depends on the failed thing.
adversarial_questions: Can authentication recover if the primary store is down?
Can repair run without the normal scheduler/queue/telemetry plane?
Are recovery dependencies acyclic or explicitly bootstrapped?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Critical recovery paths require an acyclic bootstrap or a documented dependency-reduced safe mode.

closure_axes.name: Reproducibility, hermeticity, and environment drift
closure_axes.gap: A passing run is weak evidence if dependencies, hardware, toolchains, or hidden network state cannot be reconstructed.
adversarial_questions: Can the evidence environment be recreated?
Are dependency/toolchain/model/data identities pinned?
Does the result hold on a second compatible environment?
closure_axes.stop_condition: High-impact evidence must bind environment identity and survive reproducible replay.

closure_axes.name: Long-horizon entropy and aging
closure_axes.gap: Systems fail after weeks/months through TTL expiry, counter growth, stale caches, certificate rotation, model retirement, and slow leaks.
adversarial_questions: What expires or accumulates after long uptime?
Can counters/IDs/queues/logs/indexes grow without bound?
What happens when models/providers/certs are retired mid-lifecycle?
closure_axes.stop_condition: No production claim based only on short-lived happy-path runs where aging changes semantics.

closure_axes.name: Compound-fault closure
closure_axes.gap: Independent single-fault tests do not prove safety when failures interact across authority, state, network, resources, and evidence.
adversarial_questions: Which pairwise faults invalidate a single-axis proof?
Which three-plus-axis scenarios threaten irreversible effects or trust roots?
Can recovery be replayed deterministically after compound faults?
closure_axes.stop_condition: Applicable critical compound campaigns must pass or carry explicit signed risk acceptance before production promotion.

compound_campaigns.name: Effect committed, receipt lost, retry races
compound_campaigns.oracle: Exactly one external effect; eventual authoritative receipt; no blind retry.

compound_campaigns.name: Point-in-time restore with rotated keys and newer object state
compound_campaigns.oracle: Restored state cannot revive revoked authority; external/object divergence is reconciled.

compound_campaigns.name: Partition plus lease expiry plus clock skew plus stale worker
compound_campaigns.oracle: Only current fenced owner may commit; stale worker writes are rejected.

compound_campaigns.name: Provider semantic drift during privacy-sensitive fallback
compound_campaigns.oracle: Fallback narrows or preserves privacy/authority; drift invalidates stale compatibility evidence.

compound_campaigns.name: Disk full plus telemetry backpressure plus cancellation
compound_campaigns.oracle: Control path remains bounded; terminal state is reconstructable; no corruption.

compound_campaigns.name: Cross-tenant cache collision under eviction and replay
compound_campaigns.oracle: No cross-tenant data appears; replay retains tenant identity.

compound_campaigns.name: Mid-migration rollback with old reader and new writer
compound_campaigns.oracle: Compatibility contract either preserves correctness or blocks the unsafe mixed state.

compound_campaigns.name: Trust-root compromise during repair/bootstrap
compound_campaigns.oracle: Re-root is possible without trusting compromised normal-plane state; history remains verifiable.

compound_campaigns.name: Swarm fan-out plus underestimated cost plus provider throttling
compound_campaigns.oracle: Fan-out contracts, budgets contract, and service remains fair under throttling.

compound_campaigns.name: Contaminated benchmark plus correlated verifier plus promotion pressure
compound_campaigns.oracle: Candidate cannot self-validate or promote; contamination/correlation is surfaced.

compound_campaigns.name: Interrupted installer/update with partial config and old binary
compound_campaigns.oracle: Restart reaches old-known-good or new-complete state; never an undocumented hybrid.

compound_campaigns.name: Deletion request followed by backup restore and stale derived indexes
compound_campaigns.oracle: Deletion/tombstones dominate restore and rebuild; derived state cannot resurrect deleted data.

promotion_gates.name: Applicability
promotion_gates.rule: All closure axes are classified applicable or not-applicable with rationale; silence is not N/A.

promotion_gates.name: Single-axis evidence
promotion_gates.rule: Applicable high-impact axes have executable evidence bound to the implementation artifact.

promotion_gates.name: Pairwise interaction
promotion_gates.rule: Consequential side-effect, authority, state, and rollback paths have pairwise fault coverage.

promotion_gates.name: Compound campaigns
promotion_gates.rule: Applicable CCF campaigns pass their explicit oracle or have signed risk acceptance.

promotion_gates.name: Recovery replay
promotion_gates.rule: Recovery/rollback/restore evidence is replayable from recorded manifests and does not depend on hidden operator state.

promotion_gates.name: Independent closure
promotion_gates.rule: High-impact closure evidence has independent verification and signed accountability bound to digests.

forbidden_shortcuts: aggregate green CI used to hide a failed critical obligation
planned tests counted as passing evidence
same generator output treated as independent verification
restore declared successful before external-effect and tombstone reconciliation
retry after unknown outcome without reconciliation
short soak used to waive long-horizon aging risks
manual operator knowledge used as an undocumented recovery dependency
machine/prose drift accepted without a tracked gap
single-fault testing used to waive applicable compound campaigns
implementation presence used as proof of verified behavior
